To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
infrastructureless systems are promising, but have a high potential for misuse, while infrastructure based systems are more reliable, but are not as flexible.
infrastructure based systems have the potential to provide the highest level of traffic information quality, but are also most expensive and difficult to implement.

(1) infrastructureless systems are not yet ready for deployment due to their high communication requirements, (2) infrastructure based systems relying on the peer-to-peer paradigm have a high potential to be deployed in near future, but (3) infrastructure based systems using the client-server paradigm are the most promising ones, because they can be deployed in near term with a minimum effort.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of such systems, their performance analysis and the evaluation of their impact on road users.
the design and evaluation of a vehicular based cooperative system for traffic information dissemination.

the following topics: the development of an efficient and scalable protocol for the exchange of information among vehicles, the analysis of the performance and the evaluation of the potential benefits of cooperative traffic information systems, the development of a client server based cooperative traffic information system, the design of an architecture for the exchange of cooperative traffic information between vehicles and road side infrastructure, and the design of a system for the exchange of traffic information between vehicles, road side units and traffic control centres.

the infrastructure based client server systems are the most promising ones for the future.
the most promising concept for cooperative traffic information systems is the infrastructure based client server system.

the most promising solutions are those which combine inter vehicle communication and infrastructure.
